parts.text: A student is using a forcemeter and a set of different loads to determine the weight of a metre rule. She is using the apparatus shown in Fig. 2.1. Fig. 2.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Fig. 2.2 shows the position of the load on the metre rule. The load is always at this position on the rule. Fig. 2.2 (not full size) Determine the scale reading on the metre rule at which the centre of the load is located. Show your working. scale reading = .....................................................cm [2]

ms.label: 2(a)
ms.text:
indication of taking mean reading / deducing half load length and adding or subtracting
scale reading= 70(.0)

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The student measures the force F indicated by the forcemeter for different loads placed on the rule. Figs. 2.3 (a)–(e) show the scale of the forcemeter for values of load L = 1.00 N, 2.00 N, 3.00 N, 4.00 N and 5.00 N. Fig. 2.3 In Table 2.1, record the value of F for each load. Table 2.1 L / N F / N 1.00 2.00 3.00 4.00 5.00 [2]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Plot a graph of F / N ( y -axis) against L / N ( x -axis). Start your graph at the origin (0,0). [4]

ms.label: 2(c)
ms.text:
graph:
•
axes labelled with quantity and unit
•
appropriate scales (plots occupying at least ½ grid)
•
plots all correct to ½ small square
•
well judged straight line and thin line, precise plots

parts.label: i
parts.text: (d) (i) Determine the value y of the intercept of the line on the F axis. y = ...........................................................[1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) The weight W of the metre rule is numerically equal to 2 y . Write down a value for W to a suitable number of significant figures for this experiment. W = ...........................................................[2]

ms.label: 2(d)(ii)
ms.text:
W in range 1.4 to 2.0
to 2 or 3 sig fig and with unit of N

ms.label: 2(e)
ms.text:
any suitable source on inaccuracy, e.g.:
•
rule not uniform / weight not distributed evenly,
•
load slips on rule,
•
forcemeter not at zero to start,
•
load values not exact
